I read all of Smoothing.lean (lines 1–124). It has three theorems and no @[simp] declarations, definitions or simp-set extensions, so the only question is whether the simp interface it relies on is poor.

- The only simp-set lemma it uses is `ContractionSemigroup.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup_apply`, in the `simpa only` inside `exists_contDiff_ae_eq_heatSemigroup`. In TauCeti/Analysis/Semigroups/Basic.lean (line 236) it is already `@[simp]` and proved by `rfl`, with the direction `S.toStronglyContinuousSemigroup t = S t`. That is the canonical direction and it creates no cycle.
- The Semigroup.lean API already has `heatSemigroup_zero`, `heatSemigroup_apply`, `heatSemigroup_apply_apply` and the `heatSemigroup_ae_eq_convolution*` lemmas. I did not check whether they carry simp attributes. They are conditional on `t ≠ 0` or are almost-everywhere equalities, so I would not make them simp lemmas.
- The other `simpa only` uses in the file (`toReal_enorm`, `ENNReal.toReal_inv`, `one_div`) are targeted rewrites with Mathlib lemmas, not gaps in a local simp interface.
- I found no case of unwanted expansion, a competing rule or a rewrite cycle. Without running Lean I cannot confirm that no other simp lemma in the wider library interacts with these goals.
